interactions.summary: Jiang pauses on Beatrice's distinction and asks the room to define absolute versus contingent will; a student answers with a martyrdom test in which love of God collapses under threat of death.
A student proposes that absolute will comes from imagination and one's inner story, whereas contingent will comes from reasoning through outcomes.
Jiang keeps pressing for a simpler distinction, and another student recasts the problem through moral absolutes and the novel Silence, where priests compromise under threat to protect others.

claims.claim: Jiang treats the distinction between absolute will and contingent will as a crucial interpretive key that the class must unpack before Piccarda's case can make sense.
The classroom's first pass defines absolute will as unwavering fidelity to God and contingent will as the part of the self that yields when threatened with material harm.
claims.temporal_scope: Student formulations tested and solicited by Jiang on 2026-06-15.

claims.claim: One student model, left standing by Jiang as part of the exploration, casts absolute will as imagination or story-level commitment and contingent will as logic that compares outcomes and avoids worse damage.

signature_moments.moment: A student gives Jiang a memorable split between wills by saying one comes from imagination and one's own story while the other comes from logic and comparing outcomes.
signature_moments.source_phrase: absolute will comes from imagination, it comes from your own story
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves the packet's sharpest classroom attempt to separate transcendent commitment from material calculation.

signature_moments.moment: The room drags Dante's coercion problem into a modern missionary image from Silence, where priests bend to protect others from torture.
signature_moments.source_phrase: because I don't want more harm to be done
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the abstract will distinction a vivid case of compromised fidelity under pressure.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The unyielding will the class initially describes as staying loyal to God no matter the threat.
The will that reacts to worldly threats and can yield out of fear of greater harm.
The novel a student invokes as an analogy for priests compromising religious commitment to protect persecuted believers.

chronology_notes.note: This June 15 packet is the room's exploratory pass on Beatrice's distinction, moving from martyrdom and imagination to coercion-driven compromise before Jiang gives his own cleaner model.
